title: Issue 5: transactional job transitions and pure reads

requirements.expectation: All cross-table job/payment writes, read-time repairs, provider calls, and emitted effects are mapped to explicit transaction and retry boundaries.
requirements.verification: Search table writers and call chains; record each atomic DB unit, external side effect, idempotency key, and recovery path.
evidence: Inventory identified payment/job booking, webhook intake, read-time repair, expiry, payout recovery and emitted notification/event paths; provider verification remains outside the SQL transaction.

requirements.expectation: A successful payment booking commits payment state, job state/version, status event, and required outbox work atomically, or commits none of them.
requirements.verification: Inspect SQL transaction/RPC and test rollback at each write boundary, including job cancellation/refund and stale-version races.
evidence: Unit test asserts the RPC receives the exact verified obligation and job_version. In a disposable PostgreSQL fixture, a forced outbox constraint failure rolled back payment/job writes; valid booking returned confirmed, duplicate booking returned already_confirmed, and Issue 4 trigger advanced job_version from 0 to 1.

requirements.expectation: Authenticated provider notifications are durably and idempotently accepted before acknowledgement; duplicate delivery cannot repeat the transition.
requirements.verification: Test identical and conflicting event IDs, process restart after intake, provider outage, malformed event, and acknowledgment/retry behavior.
evidence: Flutterwave webhook route is authenticated and inserts an idempotent inbox record before processing; route behavior tests pass with a mocked durable store. Database dedupe/restart evidence remains pending.

requirements.expectation: Post-commit events/notifications are recoverable after process exit and safely redelivered at least once.
requirements.verification: Crash after commit and before delivery; retry/lease expiry; verify idempotent consumers and explicit terminal/manual recovery.
evidence: Booking SQL inserts event and outbox intent in the same transaction; a disposable PostgreSQL test drained one outbox item into one event and two notifications. Lease takeover and full-schema testing remain pending.

requirements.expectation: Provider verification/refund/transfer calls stay outside DB transactions and cannot be duplicated unsafely by worker retries.
requirements.verification: Trace every external call and test durable intent, provider idempotency, uncertain outcomes, and reconciliation behavior.
evidence: Provider verification occurs before the SQL RPC; payout recovery remains in the worker via existing payout-settlement code. Provider idempotency and uncertain transfer outcomes still require hosted/test-account evidence.

requirements.expectation: Transient failures retry with bounded backoff/leases; exhausted or ambiguous financial work remains visible and recoverable rather than silently discarded.
requirements.verification: Test worker crash, repeated DB/provider outage, lease takeover, maximum retry handling, and manual recovery procedure.
evidence: Inbox/reconciliation retry bounds and attempt-matched finish calls are implemented; manual-review queue has no operator UI, and PostgreSQL lease/restart behavior remains untested.

requirements.expectation: Ordinary job reads and lists perform no payment verification, job/payment writes, notifications, or state repair.
requirements.verification: Trace getJob and list call graphs; assert read endpoints make no provider calls or mutation queries; verify reconciliation remains available independently.
evidence: getJob now returns the durable read/hydration result directly; full and lean list paths no longer call maybeExpire. Static call-site review confirms reconciliation, expiry and release repair are assigned to explicit actions or the worker.

requirements.expectation: Issue 4 job_version CAS remains intact and payment, refund, terminal-state, assignment, fee, and deadline rules are preserved.
requirements.verification: Review migration/function guards against current state-machine behavior and protected rules; run regression and concurrency tests.

requirements.expectation: Inbox/outbox tables and RPCs are inaccessible to anon/authenticated clients and the migration safely handles existing data.
requirements.verification: Apply/reapply in isolated PostgreSQL; inspect grants/RLS, indexes, data migration and rollback/recovery behavior.
evidence: Migration 080 applied successfully to a disposable PostgreSQL fixture; RLS FORCE, table grants and function execute grants were reviewed in migration SQL. Full-schema reapplication and explicit role-privilege assertions remain pending.

requirements.expectation: Durable reconciliation and outbox processing catch up without a browser and recover after overlapping runs/restarts.
requirements.verification: Record target scheduler, secret configuration, cadence, no-browser test, outage/restart evidence, and hosted monitoring separately.
evidence: Issue 3 scheduler activation and unattended hosted evidence are currently pending

implementationNotes: Transactional payment booking, durable inbox/reconciliation/outbox processing, and pure ordinary reads are implemented. Local checks and disposable PostgreSQL transaction smoke tests passed. Migration 080 was applied to the configured Supabase project and verified. Remaining work is separated under remainingWork.
